notes: NO OLD ARTIFACT WAS REWRITTEN. reports/sessions/exp-w1-opening/trace.jsonl.pin.json still records 36,000/0 with the recovery agent's divergence note inside it. NO NEW VERDICT IS FILED. This round answers the divergence and re-measures the current state. The matched >=90-minute A/B sessions, the isolated 500-word baton chain, the blind pair and the complete permissiveness population are critic-owned under the plan's sections 3.C/3.D and remain unrun.

A CONCURRENT AGENT'S REBASE DESTROYED THIS STATUS FILE, THE WRITE-UP, THE PROBE TOOL AND THE BLOG LINE about an hour into the round; the gitignored JSON artifacts survived because they were never in the index. All were rewritten from working notes and banked immediately. Nothing was measured twice or reported from memory — every number is read back out of an artifact on disk.

CONTENTION: tools/contention.mjs reported 3-5 browser instances and 4.6-6.5 load per core against a 4.0 per-core ceiling throughout (the 6-instance ceiling was reached but not exceeded). I PROCEEDED, one browser at a time, and say so here as the rule requires. Justification: every number in the divergence sections is a deterministic event count at a fixed seed, not a timing measurement — runs C and D agreeing to the event across two different trees under different load is itself the evidence that contention did not touch these figures. No wall-clock number is published anywhere in this round.

Contention did impose one real cost: the first design of the consumption probe re-applied its perturbation before every step and could not finish a 30-frame loop inside a 30-minute budget at load 6.5 per core. That is what sent me looking for the cheaper AND more faithful perturbation the tool now uses (perturb the schedule's input, not its output).

Frames are SwiftShader. No screenshot is offered in support of any claim, because every claim here is a count or a state read. The renderer check in the consumption probe reads the scene graph's own visibility flags rather than pixels, for the same reason.
tools/experience/npc-presence-consumption.mjs is a new file in tools/experience/**, which is W1-25's declared ownership; no other piece's file was edited.

The re-run after the baseline fix hit a tree that did not boot — `this._updateGrade is not a function` from another agent's in-flight renderer work, with an untracked game/src/render/post/grade.js beside it. Not this round's change. Waited for boot-check to pass and re-ran; the numbers were unchanged from the first complete run.
done: FRAMES — NOT A DIVERGENCE. session-run.mjs:323 is `totalFrames = Math.round(minutes * 60 * 60)`. The pinned manifest records minutes_requested 10 / frames_stepped 36,000; the regeneration-sample manifest records 1 / 3,600. The 10x is the one-minute sample the recovery agent deliberately took and labelled in its own pin. The frame budget has not changed and the seed still determines the world. Eliminated with certainty, and it explains nothing about the events.

COULD THE ORIGINAL RUN HAVE FIRED AT ALL? YES, DEMONSTRATED. Old tree reconstructed by `git archive 0756be2 | tar -x` into an empty directory (the last commit before the artifact's 08:15 mtime), never measured against the working tree. Same tree, same seed 1337, same first-hour profile, same brief; the ONLY change is a 15-op input script instead of --drive none. Undriven: 0 events. Driven: 4 events across 4 kinds (first_input, first_control, ACTION_START, attack_start). The old instrument could fire and did, the moment something happened in front of it. So W1-25-r1's central claim was real evidence and its score is not void.

THE POSITIVE CONTROL IS THE PLAUSIBLE WRONG ANSWER, NOT THE TRIVIAL ONE. Calling bus.emit directly from the page would have proved only that a function exists. The arm that ran is an ordinary player doing ordinary things through the ordinary input path, on the same tree, in the same profile, at the same seed.

THE PINNED TRACE'S CHANNEL WAS PRESENT, NOT ABSENT. Streaming the 79 MiB file: the events key is on every record sampled, always [], records_missing_events_key 0. So the zero is a real empty list rather than a field that did not exist yet — necessary but not sufficient, which is why the positive control above was needed.

THE 2x2 PUTS 100% OF THE EFFECT IN game/. Four runs, all --minutes 1 --seed 1337 --profile first-hour --drive none, crossing driver against game via two mixed trees. old driver + old game 0; NEW driver + old game 0; old driver + NEW game 113; new driver + new game 113. C and D are identical to the event (weather_change 1, spawn 56, settlement_enter 1, npc_schedule 28, npc_presence 27) and match the recovery agent's independently-taken 113. The driver contributes nothing; the effect is total and deterministic under the seed. Raw counts in reports/experience/w1-25-r2-divergence/session-2x2.json.

THE MECHANISM, DATED. git log -S on each emit string: npc_schedule and npc_presence first appear 08-07 13:53 (23fd1dc), settlement_enter 13:56 (b7d249a), weather_change 16:37 (38efe37) — five to eight hours AFTER the artifact's 08:15. spawn already existed (b88e439, 08-06 21:16) and fires 56 times today because there are now 56 NPCs to stream in; EventBus.clear() runs per frame and traceStart is called after world load, so the old world simply had nobody to stream.

CONSUMPTION (RI-MTH07) ON THE STATE THE NEW EVENTS MIRROR. New tool tools/experience/npc-presence-consumption.mjs. Model: sim.npcs[].present/.visible, written by stepSchedule() on the same line that emits npc_presence. Consumers named by path: game/src/render/renderer.js:548, game/src/sim/world-collision.js:121, game/src/sim/stealth/system.js:949.

THE OBVIOUS PERTURBATION WAS TOO WEAK AND IS REPORTED RATHER THAN QUIETLY DROPPED. Writing present/visible directly moves the census by exactly 1 (27 -> 26 drawn), because stepSchedule() recomputes present from n.at === sim.env.interior at the end of EVERY frame and undoes the write within one step. Publishing that as consumption evidence would have been overstating it.

THE PERTURBATION THE CLAIM RESTS ON GOES THROUGH THE MODEL'S OWN INPUT. n.at is rewritten only when the schedule SLOT changes (`if (i !== n._slot)`), so perturbing it is durable — and faithful, because the world's own code then computes the absence, emits its own npc_presence, and each consumer reads a value the world produced rather than one the probe forced in behind it. stepNPCWorldCollision runs at sim/step.js:185, immediately after stepNPCs at 182.

THE NULL ARM IS GENERIC, NOT EMPTY. An empty NPC list would collapse every observable by accident — the exact mistake that let a recent landform instrument report 71% coverage of a world containing none of the thing it measured. So the null arm restores `at` and instead perturbs `activity`: written by the same slot block, on the same objects, at the same moment, of the same shape, through the same route, and every observable must return to its intact value.

CURRENT STATE — RI-EXP02's BLOCKER HAS MOVED FROM THE FIXTURE TO THE NAMING. The still session: 36,000 frames, 0 events, 0 tellable. AND THAT ZERO CAN FIRE — CHECKED, BECAUSE IT IS THE WHOLE LESSON OF THIS ROUND. node tools/experience/anecdote-trace.mjs --self-test passes 5/5 including a `rich` case returning tellable=14, shapes=3, nouns=18. The A2 proper-noun test is not inert.

NEW FINDING — THE 121,085 IS NOT RICHNESS. 80,476 of the 121,085 events are one enemy oscillating between search_start (40,320) and search_end (20,156), alongside enemy_state (40,323) and detect (20,158) — about 3.7 search starts PER FRAME over 10,800 frames. An AI thrash defect owned by W1-12, named here so it has somewhere to be picked up. It inflates any event-count claim about this build and makes RI-EXP03's class histogram over that trace 99.9% one oscillation. The number worth publishing is 62 candidates / 0 tellable, not 121,085 events.

CURRENT STATE — RI-EXP03's unclassified_fraction: 1 IS LIVE, NOT A STALE ARTIFACT. Re-measured the cause directly at HEAD: all ten A-EXP2 event names (book_read, barter_open, barter_close, menu_open, menu_close, craft, parley, crime_witnessed, travel_node, first_visit) are 0/10 in the closed vocabulary in game/src/sim/events.js and 0/10 emitted anywhere in game/src/. A not-yet-built dependency on the UI and trade pieces, not a W1-25 defect — but the item cannot pass while it holds.

CURRENT STATE — A LIVE DEFECT FOUND IN THE TOOL'S OWN LOGS. session-run.mjs at HEAD prints on every first-hour boot: `204 of 448 harness methods refused ... 77 UNCLASSIFIED and refused fail-closed`. The same line on the old game reads `106 of 316 ... classification covers the whole surface`. 77 methods (castSpellAt, enterInterior, equipItem, commitCrime, grantInventoryItem, setPermissivenessClosure among them) have arrived since without capability declarations. The plan is explicit that a session observed with unclassified capability-bearing methods CANNOT satisfy the builder smoke — so the builder smoke cannot be satisfied today, and nothing was going red about it.

RULING (REVERSIBLE) — THE CANONICAL PATH IS THE ONE THAT COUNTS, AND IT IS STALE RATHER THAN RIGHT. matrix-probe.mjs:494 documents and defaults to reports/composition/w1/matrix.json. The remedy is to re-run the tool to that default and let the number stand or fall on that run, NOT to copy the 08-11 side artifact over it. Reversal: the side artifact is untouched and remains the record of the 08-11 run. Falsifier: a re-run to the canonical path that does NOT reproduce 12 would mean the 08-11 run was conditioned on something its manifest does not capture — the same shape as the divergence this round was opened to settle — and it would then be that run, not this ruling, that needs explaining.

CONSUMPTION RESULT — DEMONSTRATED, 6/6, with the null arm at exactly zero effect. Intact 27 drawn / 27 collidable / 27 perceivers over a population of 56 NPCs and 56 meshes. Writing present directly: 27 -> 26 (effect size 1). Perturbing the schedule's INPUT: 26 -> 0 drawn, 26 -> 0 collidable, 26 -> 0 perceivers (effect size 26), with the renderer still holding all 56 mesh objects and drawing none of them — so this is the visibility flag being read, not the scene being torn down. Null arm: back to 26/26/26, effect size 0. So the 55 new schedule/presence events per simulated minute track something a player would actually meet; they are not the sim/camera.js failure.

TWO THINGS I GOT WRONG, RECORDED RATHER THAN TIDIED AWAY. (1) The obvious perturbation was nearly inert and I nearly published it — writing `present` directly moves the census by 1, a 3.7% effect, and the honest reading of that arm is 'the probe is fighting the writer', not 'the consumer is weak'. It is kept as check C1 with its own explanation, because the gap between 1 and 26 is the lesson. (2) The null arm's first version compared against the wrong baseline and reported FAIL, 26 against INTACT's 27 — a defect in the CHECK, not the world, because the one-shot arm leaves one person absent for good when their schedule slot does not turn over inside the arm. The control for an arm is the arm that ran before it; the fix carries that reasoning in a comment beside it. Both runs are consistent; only the comparison changed.
